The longest river in the world is the Nile River.

To help understand the concept of inflation theory in cosmology, imagine a raisin bread dough rising in an oven. Before baking, the dough is small and dense, with raisins (representing galaxies) close together. As the dough bakes and expands rapidly, the space between the raisins increases dramatically. This expansion isn't the raisins moving through the dough, but rather the dough itself stretching. Similarly, during the inflation period, the fabric of space itself expanded exponentially, causing distant parts of the universe to move away from each other faster than the speed of light, much like how the distance between two raisins can increase faster than any single raisin could move on its own.
